name: Cisco XR NETCONF Lab
what_it_is: A Jupyter-based hands-on lab for learning NETCONF/YANG and building Python NETCONF clients against Cisco IOS-XR. It pairs a notebook workspace with a Docker-compose telemetry stack (InfluxDB + Telegraf + Chronograf) to visualise model-driven telemetry while exercises run.
components: Jupyter Lab notebook (workshop.ipynb) for NETCONF exercises
ncclient Python library for NETCONF RPC calls
Telegraf 1.11.5 collector ingesting gRPC telemetry from IOS-XR on port 57777
Chronograf 1.6.2 dashboard for visualising telemetry data
IOS-XR device (external, required) with NETCONF-YANG SSH agent enabled
Iperf traffic generator (installed on both Linux host and IOS-XR)
protocols: gRPC no-TLS (port 57777, model-driven telemetry streaming from IOS-XR to Telegraf)
HTTP (InfluxDB API on port 8086, Chronograf UI on port 8888)
measurement: Telemetry sample interval: 10000 ms (10 s) with strict-timer subscription
All telemetry stored in InfluxDB database named 'telemetry'
Chronograf dashboard ('Traffic Monitoring') loaded manually for visualisation
configuration: workshop-configuration.ini: [DEVICE] section with Host, SSHPort (22), NCPort (830), UserName, Password
IOS-XR requires: telemetry model-driven config, destination-group pointing to host:57777, sensor-group SGroupGeneric1, subscription Subscription1
IOS-XR requires: netconf-yang agent ssh enabled
IOS-XR requires: tpa vrf default update-source dataports Loopback0
Jupyter Lab host assumed at 198.18.134.50; IOS-XR at 198.18.134.72 (credentials: cisco/cisco)
modes: Interactive notebook mode: cells executed manually with Shift+Enter
Telemetry monitoring mode: docker-compose stack running alongside notebook exercises
constraints: Requires an external physical or virtual IOS-XR device (not included in the repo); lab does NOT provide a simulated XR instance
IOS-XR version must be 7.0.x or compatible; lab was tested only against 7.0.x
Host must be a Linux machine with a fixed IP (198.18.134.50 assumed in IOS-XR telemetry destination config)
Python version must be 3.x; tested on 3.6.8 with ncclient 0.6.6
Iperf must be installed on both the Linux host and the IOS-XR device to generate traffic for telemetry exercises
docker-compose v1.23.2 required (version 3 compose file format)
docker_services: telegraf (telegraf:1.11.5-alpine) — gRPC telemetry receiver, port 57777 exposed to host
chronograf (chronograf:1.6.2-alpine) — web UI, port 8888 exposed to host, connects to influxdb:8086
notable_absences: No simulated or containerised IOS-XR device; a real device is mandatory
No RESTCONF support documented despite IOS-XR supporting it
No gNMI/gNOI coverage despite gRPC being present for telemetry
No TLS configuration for gRPC telemetry (explicitly 'no-tls')
No automated test suite or CI pipeline
No YANG model browser or YANG explorer tooling included
